clue.text: Newly designed homes more apt to take another form

indicators.note: something newly designed has been reworked, so these letters are put into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Freshly built houses are better suited to being converted into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly designed' signals an anagram of HOMES MORE APT; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To metamorphose is to change completely in shape or nature, exactly taking another form.

clue.text: Huge area for international leader in written communication

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: a missive is a letter or written message

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of international

explanation.surface: A vast region for a global chief in correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: A (area) replaces I (the leader of 'international') in MISSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Massive means very large and heavy, a direct synonym of huge.

clue.text: In Oxford they're on two feet

definitions.text: In Oxford they're on two feet

parts.words: In Oxford they're on two feet
parts.note: Oxford is a type of laced shoe, so the clue describes protective tips sitting on the front of a pair of shoes

explanation.definitionFit: Toecaps are the reinforced fronts of shoes such as Oxfords, covering both feet.

clue.text: Can't be beaten — no game to play!

definitions.meaning: read as without a contest or fixture, a word ending in -less

explanation.surface: An unbeatable team has nobody to play against.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchless means peerless and unequalled; split, it means having no match or game.

clue.text: Be sick, seeing the poor devil executed

indicators.note: executed means beheaded, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: a wretch is a poor devil, an unfortunate person

explanation.surface: Someone feels nauseous watching an unfortunate prisoner put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' is taken as beheaded: WRETCH loses its head, W.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to heave as if vomiting, so to be sick.

clue.text: A look into hotel information could be a source of illumination

indicators.note: into means the first pieces go inside the others

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
gen is British slang for information
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Glancing at the hotel's guide might show where the lighting comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: A LO goes into H GEN; 'could be' is a link. GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A halogen lamp gives bright light, so halogen can stand for a source of illumination.

clue.text: One prepares the land by the first of September, it's less stormy

indicators.note: by means set next to, so the farmer comes beside the letter from September
the first of takes the opening letter of September

parts.note: a tiller is one who tills or prepares soil

explanation.surface: A farmer readies his fields by early September, when the weather is calmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiller means calmer, more still, the comparative of a calm-weather adjective.

clue.text: Showing initiative, but regret spin in letters

indicators.note: letters here means the words are rewritten letter by letter, a signal to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Being resourceful but writing letters full of remorseful excuses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' is an unusual anagram indicator for REGRET SPIN IN; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprising describes someone who shows initiative and resourcefulness.

clue.text: Beginning climb after hearty lunch

indicators.note: after places the climb following the letter from lunch
the heart of a word is its central letter, so the middle of lunch is wanted here

parts.note: a climb is an ascent

explanation.surface: Starting the uphill walk once you have eaten a big lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearty' looks like it describes a big meal, but it means the heart of 'lunch', its middle letter N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent describes something just coming into being, an adjective synonym of beginning.

clue.text: Everybody in associations counts

indicators.note: in places everybody inside the word for associations

parts.note: ties are connections or associations
everybody means all

explanation.surface: Each member of the societies matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallies are counts or scores kept, a plural noun synonym.

clue.text: Worried Turkish critic lost one, but made a lot of money

indicators.note: worried suggests something disturbed and churned up, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: An anxious reviewer from Turkey lost something but became wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange TURKISH CRITIC after it has 'lost' one I.
explanation.definitionFit: Struck it rich is an idiom for suddenly becoming wealthy.

clue.text: Engraving?

parts.note: read as something cut into stone over a grave: an engraving placed on a grave

explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is the inscription carved on a tombstone, literally an en-grave-ing.

clue.text: One bargains for goods in healthier surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the word for healthier is wrapped round the goods

parts.note: hale means healthy, so haler is healthier
G stands for good, doubled for the plural goods

explanation.surface: A trader haggles over goods in a more wholesome setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' and 'in' are link words; 'surroundings' is the container signal, and G for good is doubled to make the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A haggler is someone who bargains over price, so one who bargains.

clue.text: Looks for people of one's own standing

definitions.meaning: to look closely or squint at something
equals in rank or age, as in being judged by a jury of one's equals

explanation.surface: Searching for others of the same social rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers as a verb means looks intently; as a noun it means one's equals.

clue.text: Unusual European community coin starting to rise in circulation

parts.note: a cent is a small coin

indicators.note: starting to points at the opening letter of each of the last three words

explanation.surface: An odd European coin is beginning to be seen more widely in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starting to' takes the first letters of 'rise in circulation', giving RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric means odd or out of the ordinary, a direct synonym of unusual.

clue.text: Players' profit swallowed in a second by instruments

parts.note: a cast is the group of players in a play

indicators.note: swallowed in means the profit goes inside the next letters

parts.note: net profit is what is left after costs

explanation.surface: The actors' earnings were gulped down quickly by the musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Castanets are clicking percussion instruments used in Spanish dance.

clue.text: Dreamers are inclined to be trapped by thoughts

indicators.note: trapped by means caught inside the word for thoughts

parts.note: ideas are thoughts
to list is to lean or be inclined, as a ship does

explanation.surface: Visionaries tend to be imprisoned by their own notions.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealists pursue perfect visions rather than practical reality, so they are dreamers.

clue.text: Form of English developing as true unknown quantity

indicators.note: developing means changing into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: in algebra y is a standard unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A kind of English is evolving as a genuinely unknown factor.
explanation.walkthrough: Estuary English is the accent of south-east England around the Thames estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: Estuary is a British accent of English named after the Thames estuary area.

clue.text: Gave one leave due to skin blemishes

parts.note: lent means gave temporarily
the Roman numeral I is one
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone was granted time off because of a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Due to' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentigo is a medical term for a condition of small brown spots, freckle-like marks on skin.

clue.text: Dish from southern States — hot one

parts.note: the States is the US
H stands for hot, as on taps
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A spicy meal from the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with fish, an example of a dish.

clue.text: In the main, they provide support

definitions.text: In the main, they provide support

parts.words: In the main, they provide support
parts.note: the main is the sea, so this describes what keeps sailors steady on a ship

explanation.definitionFit: Sea legs are the ability to keep one's balance on board a ship at sea.

clue.text: Paces around at home — what to wear?

indicators.note: around means the paces are placed about the other piece

parts.note: steps are paces
in means at home

explanation.surface: Walking about the house, wondering what to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: Step-ins are garments or shoes that are simply stepped into, things to wear.

clue.text: Vivid impressions at first on new future, for example

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of impressions

parts.note: the future is one example of a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: Strong first impressions shape a fresh outlook on what lies ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense colours or feelings are strong and vivid, a close synonym.

clue.text: The world needs courage, start to finish

indicators.note: start to finish means the opening letter moves to the end

parts.note: heart means courage

explanation.surface: The globe requires bravery from beginning to end.
explanation.walkthrough: HEART's first letter H moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is our planet, the world we live on.

clue.text: A universal right to embrace partner's status in sport

indicators.note: embrace means the letters from A, universal and right hold the partner inside

parts.note: U is the film classification for universal
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: Everyone has the right to hold their spouse's position in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: MATE goes inside AUR, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateur is the status of a sportsperson who competes unpaid, as against a professional.

clue.text: Not doing so much to chase good tradesman

indicators.note: chase means follow behind, so the idler word comes after G

parts.note: lazier means doing less work

explanation.surface: A workman who slacks off more in pursuit of quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazier fits glass in windows, an example of a tradesman.

clue.text: Mournful English adopted by version of Gaelic

indicators.note: adopted by means taken into the rearranged letters
a version of a word is a reworked form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sad English word is taken over into an Irish rendering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Version of' rearranges GAELIC to ELGIAC, and 'adopted by' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac means having the sorrowful tone of an elegy, a lament, so mournful.

clue.text: Supposes and hopes his stye gets treated

indicators.note: something treated is worked on and changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man hopes his eye infection will be dealt with by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets treated' rearranges HOPES HIS STYE; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To hypothesise is to put forward a theory, so it means supposes.
